name: Kṛṣṇa
summary: The teacher (śrī bhagavān) of the Bhagavad Gītā, Arjuna's charioteer, who blows the conch Pāñcajanya (1.15). In ch. 1–3 he rebukes Arjuna's faintness, teaches the imperishable embodied one, the argument from svadharma, the yoga of understanding and the one of steady wisdom, action for sacrifice and for holding the world together, and the conquest of desire; he says he taught the twofold commitment of old (3.3), that he has nothing to attain yet acts (3.22–24), and that all actions are to be renounced in him (3.30).

name: Arjuna
summary: Son of Pāṇḍu and Kuntī, bearer of the bow Gāṇḍīva and the conch Devadatta (1.15, 1.30); the disciple of the Gītā. In ch. 1–3 he sees his kin in both armies, is overcome by compassion and despondency, argues against the battle and says he will not fight (1.28–2.9), declares himself Kṛṣṇa's disciple (2.7), and asks about the one of steady wisdom (2.54), why action is urged if understanding is superior (3.1–2), and what drives a person to sin (3.36).

name: Sañjaya
summary: Narrator of the Gītā to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, reporting what was said and done on the battlefield (1.2–47; 2.1, 2.9–10).

name: Dhṛtarāṣṭra
summary: Father of the Kauravas ('my people', 1.1); his question to Sañjaya opens the Gītā, and Sañjaya's narration is addressed to him ('lord of the earth', 'Bhārata').

name: Duryodhana
summary: Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, king of the Kaurava side (rājā, 1.2), who names the leading warriors of both armies to his teacher and urges that Bhīṣma be protected (1.2–11); Arjuna calls him the evil-minded son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra (1.23).

name: Droṇa
summary: The teacher (ācārya), 'best of the twice-born', to whom Duryodhana speaks (1.2–11) and whose disciple Dhṛṣṭadyumna arrayed the Pāṇḍava army (1.3); with Bhīṣma one whom Arjuna holds worthy of worship (1.25, 2.4).
notes: That the ācārya of 1.2–11 is Droṇa is the epic context; Droṇa is named at 1.25 and 2.4. Linked in BhG ch. 1–3 at 1.2, 1.3, 1.7, 1.8, 1.25, 2.4.

name: Bhīṣma
summary: The aged Kuru grandsire, guardian of the Kaurava army (1.10–11), whose lion-roar and conch start the tumult (1.12); Arjuna holds him worthy of worship (2.4).

name: Karṇa
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the leaders of his (the Kaurava) army (1.8).

name: Kṛpa
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the leaders of his (the Kaurava) army, 'victorious in battle' (1.8).

name: Aśvatthāman
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the leaders of his (the Kaurava) army (1.8).

name: Vikarṇa
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the leaders of his (the Kaurava) army (1.8).

name: Bhūriśravas
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the leaders of his (the Kaurava) army as Saumadatti, 'son of Somadatta' (1.8).
notes: Saumadatti = Bhūriśravas is the epic identification. Linked in BhG ch. 1–3 at 1.8.

name: Somadatta
summary: Named only through his son's patronymic Saumadatti (1.8).

name: Dhṛṣṭadyumna
summary: Son of Drupada and Droṇa's intelligent disciple, who arrayed the Pāṇḍava army (1.3); blows his conch (1.17).
notes: Identified as the drupadaputra of 1.3 by the epic context. Linked in BhG ch. 1–3 at 1.3, 1.17.

name: Drupada
summary: A great chariot-warrior on the Pāṇḍava side (1.4), father of the army's arranger (1.3), who blows his conch (1.18).

name: Bhīma
summary: Pāṇḍava of terrible deeds who blows the great conch Pauṇḍra (1.15); the Pāṇḍava force is 'guarded by Bhīma' (1.10), and its heroes are 'equal to Bhīma and Arjuna' (1.4).

name: Yuyudhāna
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the heroes of the Pāṇḍava army (1.4); as Sātyaki, 'the unconquered', he blows his conch (1.17).
notes: Yuyudhāna = Sātyaki is the epic identification. Linked in BhG ch. 1–3 at 1.4, 1.17.

name: Virāṭa
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the heroes of the Pāṇḍava army (1.4); blows his conch (1.17).

name: Dhṛṣṭaketu
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the heroes of the Pāṇḍava army (1.5).

name: Cekitāna
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the heroes of the Pāṇḍava army (1.5).

name: The king of Kāśī (Kāśirāja)
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the heroes of the Pāṇḍava army, 'valiant' (1.5); as Kāśya, 'supreme archer', he blows his conch (1.17).
notes: The kāśirāja of 1.5 and the kāśya of 1.17 are taken as the same person. Linked in BhG ch. 1–3 at 1.5, 1.17.

name: Purujit
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the heroes of the Pāṇḍava army (1.5).

name: Kuntibhoja
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the heroes of the Pāṇḍava army (1.5).

name: Śaibya
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the heroes of the Pāṇḍava army, 'bull among men' (1.5).

name: Yudhāmanyu
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the heroes of the Pāṇḍava army, 'valiant' (1.6).

name: Uttamaujas
summary: Named by Duryodhana among the heroes of the Pāṇḍava army, 'valiant' (1.6).

name: Abhimanyu
summary: The son of Subhadrā (Saubhadra), a great chariot-warrior on the Pāṇḍava side (1.6), 'mighty-armed', who blows his conch (1.18).
notes: Saubhadra = Abhimanyu is the epic identification. Linked in BhG ch. 1–3 at 1.6, 1.18.

name: Subhadrā
summary: Mother of Saubhadra; named only through her son's metronymic (1.6, 1.18).

name: The sons of Draupadī (Draupadeyas)
summary: A group: the sons of Draupadī, great chariot-warriors on the Pāṇḍava side (1.6) who blow their conches (1.18).
notes: A group, not a single person; the Gītā does not name them individually. Linked in BhG ch. 1–3 at 1.6, 1.18.

name: Draupadī
summary: Mother of the Draupadeyas; named only through her sons' metronymic (1.6, 1.18).

name: Yudhiṣṭhira
summary: King, son of Kuntī, who blows the conch Anantavijaya (1.16).

name: Nakula
summary: Pāṇḍava who, with Sahadeva, blows the conches Sughoṣa and Maṇipuṣpaka (1.16).

name: Sahadeva
summary: Pāṇḍava who, with Nakula, blows the conches Sughoṣa and Maṇipuṣpaka (1.16).

name: Śikhaṇḍin
summary: A great chariot-warrior on the Pāṇḍava side who blows his conch (1.17).
notes: The Gītā uses the masculine; the epic tells that Śikhaṇḍin was born female. Linked in BhG ch. 1–3 at 1.17.

name: Kuntī
summary: Mother of Yudhiṣṭhira (kuntīputra, 1.16) and of Arjuna, whom Kṛṣṇa addresses as Kaunteya, 'son of Kuntī' (1.27; 2.14 and passim).

name: Pāṇḍu
summary: Father of the Pāṇḍavas, named in 'the sons of Pāṇḍu' (1.1, 1.3) and in Arjuna's epithet Pāṇḍava (1.14, 1.20).

name: Janaka
summary: Named by Kṛṣṇa as the first of those who attained perfection (saṃsiddhi) by action (3.20).

name: Prajāpati
summary: The creator who, having created beings together with sacrifice, told them to multiply by it and to nourish the gods, who would nourish them in turn (3.10–12).
